Author: Rakesh Thapliyal
Bench: Rakesh Thapliyal

 Aba No. 768 of 2025
 Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1.
Mr. M.C. Pant and Mr. D.S. Mehta, learned counsel for the applicant.
2. Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned A.G.A. with Mr. Chitrarth Kandpal, learned Brief Holder for the State.

3. The applicant 'Narendra Kumar Sharma' is praying for anticipatory bail in reference to First Information Report dated 03.02.2023 bearing FIR No. 0049 of 2023 P.S. Kotwali, District Dehradun, wherein, three persons including the present applicant namely Narendra Kumar Sharma,
Shankar Thapa and Sandeep Kapoor were implicated for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 409 r/w 120B of IPC.
On completion of the investigation the chargesheet has been filed for the offences punishable under Sections 409, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120B of IPC, P.S. Kotwali, District Dehradun.
4. The allegation as alleged is that by impersonating 17 loans were sanctioned causing the huge loss to the Bank for an amount of Rs. 47 lakhs.

5. It is argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that earlier the applicant challenged the FIR in WPCRL No. 327 of 2023 in which the interim protection was granted with the direction that the investigation may go on, however, the applicant shall not be arrested provided he cooperate with the investigation.

He submits that he always complied with the direction of the Hon'ble Court and cooperate with the investigation, however, on completion of the investigation now the chargesheet has been filedand as such is praying for anticipatory bail.

ABA/768/2025 on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75579109/
1 6.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the Coordinate Bench in another set of matters relating to different FIR granted anticipatory bail, copy of which is enclosed as Annexure-17 and 18.
7.
I have gone through peruse the order passed by the Coordinate Bench.

8. On the other side, learned A.G.A. Mr. Tumul Nainwal submits that after thorough and collecting credible evidences the charge-sheet has been filed, which constitute the cognizable offence against the applicant.
He further submits that merely grant of interim protection in the earlier criminal writ petition in which the FIR was challenged the applicant is not entitle for anticipatory bail.

He further submits that the applicant is praying for anticipatory bail on an apprehension of arrest but he submits there is no apprehension of arrest from the side of the investigation agency since the charge-sheet has been filed in the court after collecting all credible evidence.

He further argued that the applicant is not remediless he can challenge the proceeding by way of preferring the petition under Section 528 of BNSS, 2023 or to move a discharge application in the Trial Court or to challenge the order taking cognizance on the charge- sheet by way of a revision but is not entitle for anticipatory bail.

9. Apart from this, he also submits though in another set of allegation relating to the different FIR the Coordinate Bench granted anticipatory bail but merely on the ground that the Coordinate Bench has granted anticipatory bail the applicant cannot claim anticipatory bail as the allegations as alleged are different that too with regard to fake loan.

10. I prima-facie found force on the submissions as advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant since after thorough investigation and furthermore after collecting all credible evidences the charge-sheet has been filed and as such the submissions with regard to the apprehension of arrest that too after the charge- sheet prima-facie appears to be baseless.

11. In response to this, learned counsel for the applicant submits that in reference to the same set of charges the departmental proceeding was initiated and the applicant was given charge-sheet and he has given the response and during disciplinary proceeding the person, who have been given the loan deposited the maximum amount.

12. He prays for and is granted two weeks' time to file supplementary affidavit bringing on record the relevant documents relating to disciplinary proceedings initiated against the present applicant.
13. List this matter on 30.07.2025.
14. In the meantime, the respondents may also file their counter affidavit.

(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 09.07.2025 PR ABA/768/2025 on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75579109/
